newsitem.title: GERMANY: Kinkel accuses Afghan Taleban of "mob justice".
newsitem.headline: Kinkel accuses Afghan Taleban of "mob justice".

text.p: Germany's Foreign Minister Klaus Kinkel on Tuesday criticised the Afghan Taleban militia, which took the capital Kabul last Friday, for what he called "mob justice" and violating women's basic rights.

In an interview with the German daily newspaper Express, Kinkel urged the Taleban, which now controls three-quarters of Afghanistan, and other warring factions to negotiate a ceasefire under United Nations mediation.

"Afghanistan is bleeding. Civil war has nearly destroyed the whole country," Kinkel said. "With mob justice and the violation of women's basic rights, the Taleban announced it was setting up a religious state."
"Firstly, there should be an immediate ceasefire to end this civil war which has raged since 1992," Kinkel said.

"The Taleban must work closely with the U.N. envoy to Afghanistan, Norbert Holl. All civil war parties are urged to come to the negotiating table for U.N. mediated peace talks," he told the newspaper.
The Taleban, set up two years ago, is a Sunni Moslem movement which grew out of religious schools in refugee camps in neighbouring Pakistan.

Last week its militias took Kabul, snatched former president Najibullah who had been under U.N. protection and hanged him before setting up an interim ruling council vowing to turn Afghanistan into an Islamic state.

They have barred women from workplaces and told them not to leave their homes without wearing the Islamic veil. They also ordered men employed in government offices and the military to grow long beards.
